text:
Maya (growth): Quick sync: I built a compact pricing micro-calculator prototype for the pricing page. It estimates monthly bill = (avg_tokens_per_request * requests_per_minute * minutes_per_day * 30) * $per_1k_tokens_rate. Added a small "burst" slider to simulate short spikes. Want to run a small canary and test copy variants + tier labels.
Owen (design): Nice. Screenshot? also can we keep the UI minimal - inline help only, no modal.
Maya (growth): attached mock (not in thread). key UX: "burst" default 1x, optional 3x/5x. shows "estimated monthly + potential overage".
Priya (product): what's the copy for the overage note? we need something that reduces surprise but isn't legalese.
Maya (growth): current: "Short bursts above your reserved capacity may incur overage fees at the metered rate." simple.
Jules (sales): add lead tagging please: pricing_microcalc_v2 + variant tag. If a lead completes calc and opens contact form -> auto create lead in SFDC with calc inputs. High ARR leads flagged.
Luca (analytics): I'll fire two GA events: `pricing_calc_started` and `pricing_calc_submitted`. Also capture `burst_multiplier` and `tier_variant`. We'll tie to conversion funnel in Looker.
Owen (design): tier name alternatives to test (A/B): Option A: Kickstart / Scale / Enterprise Pro. Option B: Basic / Team / Enterprise. shorter labels vs familiar ones.
Priya (product): prefer Kickstart/Scale/Enterprise Pro for A, Basic/Team/Enterprise for B. Also want a control group with current names. Plan: 1) canary 5% for 24h to validate tracking 2) then 7-day A/B across 50% traffic.
Maya (growth): agreed. metrics: calc completion rate, contact form CTR, contact form conversion -> MQL. Also track page scroll depth and time-on-page to detect confusion.
Luca (analytics): suggested success metric: 1) increase calculator-to-contact CTR by 8% vs control, 2) maintain or improve time-on-page <-> we want shorter time if they convert faster.
Jules (sales): also capture "estimated_monthly" field into lead record so AEs can triage.
Maya (growth): Ops ask: can we let users toggle between "monthly estimate" and "commitment pricing"? commit mode should show discount and commit term selector.
Priya (product): doable. commitment mode will apply discount rate and show "estimated committed monthly" vs "metered monthly". We'll need clear FAQ lines to explain proration and trial credit behavior.
Maya (growth): FAQ draft for the page (please edit):
`Q: If I commit, how does billing work? A: Committed plans are billed monthly at your reserved capacity rate. Unused reserved units can roll over as credits for the next billing period. Short trial credits are applied before charges on first invoice.`
Owen (design): voice ok but let's shorten: "Unused reserved units roll over as credits for the next month." cut the legal words.
Luca (analytics): for the A/B tag remember to persist `tier_variant=A|B|control` in the lead capture payload. We'll need that for lift analysis.
marketing-bot: Reminder: pricing-microcalc-canary job scheduled 2025-09-01T09:00Z.
Maya (growth): Ops checklist: create lead webhook -> SFDC mapping, GA events + Looker dashboard, Segment trait for `pricing_microcalc_v2`.
Jules (sales): I'll prepare a short AE checklist and post in #sales-inbound. If high ARR + calc_submitted -> immediate AE ping.
Priya (product): final timeline: today: copy + analytics wiring. Tomorrow 09:00 UTC deploy 5% canary for 24h. If events look clean, roll to AB for 7 days.
Owen (design): one micro copy ask: change "burst" label to "spike" — customers understand spikes better.
Maya (growth): done. updated UI text to "spike multiplier".
Luca (analytics): will create Looker tiles: calc start rate, completion rate, contact CTA CTR, MQL rate, revenue per visitor. Sharing dashboard link once created.
Maya (growth): thanks everyone. moving PR to review. Notifying Ops to create SFDC mapping now.
Jules (sales): pre-alerting EAs in 10m.
Priya (product): thumbs up. excited to see lift. :chart_with_upwards_trend:
